Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

moment noun

a point in time

also at that moment, at the right moment, the moment (that), just in time

classical

Ter. Heaut. 2.3.123: in tempore ad eam vēnī (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 1.27: ad tempus, for the moment (Lewis & Short)

tempus, temporis n.

noun, third declension

the moment, the time (for something)

in tempore, at the right moment, just in time; ad tempus, on time, or for the moment; the very moment takes ipse (see just, exactly). “At the moment”, now, is nunc or in praesentiā (see now).

Examples

  • Pater, opportūnē advenīs.

    Father, you’ve come at just the right moment.Ter. Heaut. 179

  • quīn simul ac prōmīseris minerval, incipiam

    why, I’ll begin the moment you’ve promised my feeVarr. RR 3.2.18

Other words

  • opportūnē — at just the right moment

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 179: Pater, opportūnē advenīs.; Ter. Ad. 81: Ehem, opportūnē

  • ut prīmum (cum prīmum, simul ac) — the moment (that), as soon as

    also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 104.6: ut prīmum gravitātem urbis excessī; Varr. RR 3.2.18: simul ac prōmīseris; Liv. 21.1.4: cum prīmum posset; Traupman 88: as soon as, cum prīmum

See also moment, now, just, in good time.
